result:
If I could change the world in just one way, I’d erase the structural barriers that keep people trapped in cycles of poverty and inequality. Imagine a world where every child, regardless of where they’re born, has guaranteed access to nutritious food, clean water, safe shelter, a high‑quality education, and reliable healthcare. Those basic needs would be met not through charity or luck, but as a universally upheld right—financed by a transparent, globally coordinated system that redirects resources from wasteful excesses toward those essential services.

When those foundations are secure, countless other problems start to melt away: crime rates drop, public health improves, innovation flourishes because more minds can focus on creativity rather than survival, and the social fabric becomes richer and more resilient. In short, leveling the playing field at the most fundamental level would unleash humanity’s collective potential and give us a much stronger platform to tackle the other challenges we face.
